title: Mine manager fined for stealing from employer, assaulting worker.
desc:
Fortune Makoni fortunemakoni21@gmail.com.
A 40-YEAR-OLD mine manager in Inyathi, Bubi District has been fined US$1 000 and ordered to pay back US$1 221 to his employer after stealing company funds and assaulting a subordinate.
Zhao Rui Jun, who was employed as a factory manager at Ming Chang Sino Africa Pvt Ltd’s Lime
Factory at Turk Mine, was convicted of theft and assault by Inyathi magistrate Mr Challenge Mahembe.
For the theft charge, Zhao was fined US$1 000 or 12 months in prison.
He was sentenced to a further 12 months’ imprisonment which was suspended on condition that he restitutes his employer US$ 1 221 by September 30.
For assault, Zhao was sentenced to six months in prison, which was suspended for five years on condition that he does not commit a similar offence during that period.
The court heard that between December last year and May this year, Zhao unlawfully converted
US$3 850 belonging to his employer to his personal use.
According to the State, Zhao was responsible for production at the lime factory and had produced about 450 tonnes of quarry material valued at US$4 500.
He handed US$1 900 to the company cashier and pocketed the remaining US$2 600.
The court further heard that during the same period, Zhao leased company equipment, including a front-end loader and grader, to a garage in Inyathi and received US$2 000 in cash.
“Only US$750 was recorded in the company books, while Zhao converted the remaining US$1 250 to his own use,” read court papers.
The theft was discovered after other employees reported the theft to management, leading to Zhao’s arrest.
The court heard that US$2 629 of the stolen money was recovered.
The assault charge arose from an altercation with a subordinate, Mr Kelvin Rakata, a stone crusher operator.
On May 8, Zhao confronted Mr Rakata after he refused to increase the speed of the machine because its conveyor belt was worn out.
Zhao then ordered Mr Rakata to report to his office, where he instructed him to sign a final warning.
The court heard that while in the office, Zhao grabbed Mr Rakata by the neck before pushing him out.
A report was made to the police, leading to Zhao’s arrest.

title: Smekalicious returns home with new album Inamba
desc:
Mthokozisi Ncube mthokoncube3015@gmail.com
Bulawayo-born Amapiano musician and MC Peacemaker Mpala, popularly known as Smekalicious, is set to release his latest album, Inamba, on August 31 as he returns to Zimbabwe after spending more than a decade pursuing his music career in South Africa.
The independent artiste, who has carved a niche for himself in Amapiano and Kwaito genres, said he was now focused on reconnecting with audiences in his home country while building on the experience he gained across the Limpopo.
[caption id=attachment_5491175 align=aligncenter width=199] Peacemaker Mpala aka Smekalicious[/caption]
Smekalicious who was bred in Iminyela, popularly known as Number 1, grew up listening to Kwaito music. He was raised by a Christian family where music was an integral part of church life, an environment he credits for nurturing his passion for music.
He initially entered the entertainment industry as a Kwaito dancer before launching his music career in 2011.
“I grew up listening to Kwaito music with the likes of Mapaputsi, Kabelo, MaGesh, Zola 7, as well as Brown Dash, playing a role in inspiring me. I come from a Christian family where everyone used to sing in the church. That is where I got my love and passion for music.
“In 2011, I decided to go professional as a dancer. I did this deliberately because I wanted to understand the music game from a background perspective. After learning a few tricks, in 2014, I took a break from performing only to return in the game as a musician in 2016, as I dropped my first album titled Omapakitsha,” he said.
[caption id=attachment_5491180 align=aligncenter width=200] Peacemaker Mpala aka Smekalicious[/caption]
Smekalicious said Inamba was part of his efforts to strengthen his presence in Zimbabwe while bringing home the experience he gained during his years in South Africa.I
“Before dropping Inamba, I released an AmaPiano single titled S’groover Nabo Makhe, where I featured South African producer and DJ Visca. This single works properly as a teaser to my upcoming album because it reflects the kind of sound I will project on Inamba,” he said.
[caption id=attachment_5491185 align=aligncenter width=200] Peacemaker Mpala aka Smekalicious[/caption]
Beyond music, Smekalicious is into fashion designing, which he expresses his craft through his clothing brand named S/O (Smekalicious Omapakisha), which he said was inspired by his appreciation for his supporters.
Throughout his musical career, Smekalicious has shared the stage with several prominent artistes, including Oskido, DJ Vetkook & Mahoota, Mgarimbe, Bekezela, Platform One, Freddy Gwala, Vigro
Deep, Daliwonga, Shota, Drumpope and Visca, to mention a few.
